sources.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI, Pydantic and Uvicorn

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run hello world
steps.instructions: Run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, create main.py with `app = FastAPI()` and a `@app.get("/")` root function returning {"Hello": "World"}. Start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and open http://127.0.0.1:8000.

targets.caption: Create the FastAPI app instance
Decorator defining the GET route for the root path
Server is up at http://127.0.0.1:8000

explanations.topic: Why Uvicorn is needed: it's the server that runs FastAPI apps
Path operation decorator @app.get defines a GET route
The "/" path is the root route that calls the function
uvicorn main:app syntax and the --reload flag

hints: Install both packages: FastAPI is the framework, Uvicorn is the server that runs it.
In main.py, import FastAPI, create app = FastAPI(), then decorate a function with @app.get("/") that returns a dict.
Run uvicorn main:app --reload from the folder containing main.py; 'main' is the file name and 'app' is the variable name.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser; you should see {"Hello":"World"}.
common_mistakes: Installing only fastapi and getting 'uvicorn: command not found'.
Running uvicorn from a different directory than main.py, causing 'Could not import module "main"'.
Mismatching the app name, e.g. naming the variable api but running main:app ('Attribute "app" not found').
Writing @app.get without the leading slash or forgetting to call FastAPI() with parentheses.
Typing 'uvicorn main.py:app' instead of 'uvicorn main:app'.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint for items
steps.instructions: In main.py add a module-level `items = []` list and a `@app.post("/items")` function `create_item(item: str)` that appends the item and returns the list. With uvicorn running, test with `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'`.

targets.caption: Module-level list holding the items
POST endpoint at /items
Current items list returned by the endpoint

explanations.topic: What routes are in FastAPI
Using a list as in-memory storage
Function args become query parameters
Returning the whole list to see results
Testing with curl and a query string

hints: Create an empty list at module level (outside any function) so it persists between requests.
Decorate a function with @app.post("/items") and give it a parameter `item: str`; FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Inside the function call items.append(item) and return items.
With uvicorn running (--reload), run in a second terminal: curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'
common_mistakes: Defining items = [] inside the function, so the list resets on every request.
Using @app.get instead of @app.post, so curl -X POST returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
Forgetting the ?item=... query string, giving a 422 'field required' error.
Not quoting the URL in the shell, so ? or & get interpreted by the shell.
Uvicorn not running with --reload (or not restarted), so the new route returns 404.

steps.title: Get item by path parameter
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` with `get_item(item_id: int)` returning `items[item_id]`. Re-add items (the list resets on reload), curl /items/0, then see /items/3 return an internal server error.

targets.caption: New GET endpoint with a path parameter in curly braces
Type hint lets FastAPI convert the path value to int
Requesting a missing index crashes with a 500

explanations.topic: Path parameters: /items/{item_id} binds the URL segment to a function argument
Server reload resets the in-memory items list; re-add items before testing
Path value becomes the function variable of the same name
Type hints make FastAPI convert the path parameter type
Accessing a nonexistent index yields an internal server error

hints: Use the same @app.get decorator, but put the variable part of the path in curly braces: /items/{item_id}.
The function argument name must match the name inside the braces, and add an int type hint so it can index a list.
After saving, the server reloads and the items list is empty again; POST a couple of items first, then GET /items/0.
Try an index past the end of the list (like /items/3) and look at the uvicorn terminal: an IndexError / 500 is expected for now.
common_mistakes: Argument name differs from the {placeholder} in the path, so FastAPI treats it as a query parameter instead.
Omitting the int type hint, so item_id is a string and items[item_id] raises a TypeError.
Testing GET /items/0 right after saving without re-adding items, since the reload emptied the list.
Using parentheses or a colon instead of curly braces for the path parameter (e.g. /items/:item_id).
Thinking the 500 on /items/3 is a bug in your code; it is the expected behavior at this step, fixed in the next one.

steps.title: Raise 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: In main.py import HTTPException from fastapi and in get_item return the item if item_id < len(items), else raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...). Re-run the out-of-range curl to see the 404 detail.

targets.caption: Import HTTPException from fastapi at the top
Return the item if it exists, otherwise raise a 404
Re-run the out-of-range request to see the 404 detail

explanations.topic: Why an internal server error isn't helpful for missing items
Standard HTTP status codes; missing item is a client error
404 Not Found is the right response here
The detail parameter adds context to the error

hints: Add HTTPException to your existing `from fastapi import ...` line.
In get_item, check `if item_id < len(items):` before indexing the list, and return the item inside that branch.
In the else branch: `raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found")`.
Make sure uvicorn reloaded (run with --reload or restart it), then repeat the curl with an index larger than your list.
common_mistakes: Using `return HTTPException(...)` instead of `raise`, which returns the exception object rather than a 404 response.
Forgetting to import HTTPException, causing a NameError and still a 500.
Using `<=` instead of `<` in the bounds check, so item_id == len(items) still triggers an IndexError.
Not restarting or reloading the uvicorn server, so the old handler still returns Internal Server Error.
Forgetting the `f` prefix so the detail literally shows `{item_id}`.

steps.title: List items with limit query
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items")` with `list_items(limit: int = 10)` returning `items[0:limit]`. Test with `curl -X GET 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'`.

targets.caption: list_items endpoint with a limit query parameter
Request the first 3 items

explanations.topic: FastAPI converts query string values to the annotated int type
limit selects how many items to return, default 10
Same /items path, different HTTP method routes to a different function
Omitting limit uses the default from the function signature

hints: Add a new GET route on the same /items path you POST to.
Give the function a parameter `limit: int = 10`. Because it is not in the path, FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Return a slice of your list: `items[0:limit]`.
POST a few items first, then run `curl -X GET 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'`.
common_mistakes: Using curl without -X GET or quoting the URL, so the shell interprets the `?`.
Testing against a list that is still empty because the server restarted. Add items again before you call GET.
Forgetting the `: int` annotation, so limit stays a string and slicing fails with a TypeError.
Putting limit in the path (`/items/{limit}`) instead of using it as a query parameter.
Defining the function with the same name as the POST handler, which overwrites it.

steps.title: Use a Pydantic Item model
steps.instructions: In main.py import BaseModel from pydantic, define class Item(BaseModel) with text: str and is_done: bool = False, make create_item take item: Item and get_item return Item. POST JSON with curl and confirm a payload without text fails validation.

targets.caption: Pydantic model for a to-do item
create_item now takes the model from the JSON body
Response is an object conforming to Item

explanations.topic: Pydantic models structure data and add validation
Modeled arguments are read from the JSON payload, not query params
Default value fills is_done when omitted
Removing a default makes a field required and validated

hints: Import BaseModel from pydantic and subclass it to make Item with a str field and a bool field defaulting to False.
Change create_item's parameter type from str to Item, and annotate get_item with -> Item.
Send the data as JSON with -H 'Content-Type: application/json' and -d '{"text":"apple"}', with no ?item= query string.
To test validation, send '{"title":"apple"}'; with no default on text you should get a 422 'Field required' error.
common_mistakes: Still sending the item as a ?item=apple query parameter, which now returns a 422 error.
Forgetting the Content-Type: application/json header in curl.
Leaving a default on text (e.g. text: str = None) so missing text isn't rejected.
Using single quotes inside the JSON body, making it invalid JSON.
Not restarting uvicorn (no --reload) so the old string-based endpoint still runs.

steps.title: Add response models to routes
steps.instructions: In main.py, add `response_model=Item` to the get_item decorator and `response_model=list[Item]` to the list_items decorator. Restart uvicorn and verify the endpoints still respond.

targets.caption: Add response_model=Item to the get_item decorator
Use list[Item] as the response model for listing items

explanations.topic: Reusing the Pydantic BaseModel to describe responses
response_model is an argument on the route decorator
Declaring a list of models as the response
Response models tell clients what shape the endpoint returns

hints: The response model goes in the decorator (@app.get(...)), not in the function signature.
Pass the keyword argument response_model= with the same Item class you used for the request body.
For the endpoint that returns many items, wrap the class: response_model=list[Item].
Save main.py, then check that uvicorn reloads and that /items and /items/0 still return JSON.
common_mistakes: Putting response_model on the function parameters instead of in @app.get(...).
Writing response_model=Item on list_items, which fails validation because a list is returned.
Using list[Item] on Python older than 3.9 instead of List[Item] imported from typing.
Returning plain strings or dicts that don't match Item's fields, which causes a ResponseValidationError.
Forgetting to save or restart, so the server keeps running the old code.

steps.title: Explore interactive API docs
steps.instructions: With `uvicorn main:app --reload` running, open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, use 'Try it out' on POST /items and Execute. Also visit /redoc and /openapi.json.

targets.caption: Click 'Try it out' on POST /items
Execute and check the response body
Link to the raw OpenAPI schema

explanations.topic: FastAPI auto-generates interactive docs for free
Swagger UI at /docs lists endpoints, methods and parameters
Execute shows the curl command and sends a real request
/redoc is an alternative docs view
openapi.json describes all paths, schemas and responses

hints: Make sure your uvicorn server is still running, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in the browser.
Expand the POST /items endpoint, click 'Try it out', edit the request body, then click 'Execute'.
Scroll down below Execute to see the curl command and the server's response body.
Try /redoc and the /openapi.json link near the top of the docs page too.
common_mistakes: Opening /docs while the uvicorn server is stopped, so the page won't load.
Forgetting to click 'Try it out', so the request body stays read-only.
Sending a request body that doesn't match the Pydantic Item model, which gives a 422 validation error.
Typing the URL with a trailing typo like /doc instead of /docs.
